language_wrapper: Triangle ABC has side lengths AB={ab}, AC={ac}, and BC={bc}. Let I be the incenter of triangle ABC, and let I_ext be the A-excenter (the excenter opposite vertex A). Through I draw the line parallel to BC, meeting AB at D and AC at E; through I_ext draw the line parallel to BC, meeting the (possibly extended) lines AB at U and AC at V. Let DE = m/n and UV = p/q be the respective lengths written in lowest terms (with m,n and p,q positive and coprime). Find m + n + p + q.
hardness_rationale: This family elevates the original problem by requiring the solver to handle two parallel-cut segments tied to distinct special points (the incenter and the A-excenter) and to combine them through number-theoretic reduction. The key similarity-homothety insight from the seed (mapping BC to a parallel line via a homothety centered at A) must be generalized to points along the A-angle bisector with different radii relationships (r and r_a). The solver must derive and apply the angle-bisector length formula, inradius/exradius formulas, and homothety scaling AP/AY, then carry out rational simplifications for two distinct expressions. This introduces multiple interlocking steps and edge cases (e.g., excenter yielding an external segment), making the process more complex than the seed while preserving the core geometric idea.
notes:
Proof of correctness: Let A be the vertex common to sides AB and AC, and denote a=BC, b=AC, c=AB, with semiperimeter s=(a+b+c)/2. Consider any point P on the A-angle bisector, and draw the line through P parallel to BC intersecting AB and AC (possibly extended) at a segment of length L(P). Because triangles ADE and ABC are homothetic with center A, the parallel line is the image of BC under the homothety of factor t, so L(P)=t·a. For a specific point P on that parallel line, it is the image of the unique point Y on BC collinear with A and P, hence t = AP/AY. In particular, taking Y as the intersection of the A-angle bisector with BC, the length AY equals the A-angle bisector length l_a = 2bc·cos(A/2)/(b+c). The distances along the bisector to centers tangent to AB and AC satisfy AP = r/sin(A/2) for the incenter I (since r = AI·sin(A/2)), and AP = r_a/sin(A/2) for the A-excenter I_ext (since the excenter has perpendicular distance r_a to AB and AC). Using Δ = (1/2)bc·sin A and r = Δ/s, we get t_in = (r/sin(A/2)) / (2bc·cos(A/2)/(b+c)) = r(b+c)/(bc·sin A) = [(1/2)bc·sin A / s]·(b+c)/(bc·sin A) = (b+c)/(a+b+c), hence DE = a·(b+c)/(a+b+c). Similarly, with r_a = Δ/(s-a) = (1/2)bc·sin A/(s-a), we get t_ex = (r_a/sin(A/2)) / (2bc·cos(A/2)/(b+c)) = (b+c)/(2(s-a)) = (b+c)/(b+c-a), so UV = a·(b+c)/(b+c-a). These formulas are symmetric, consistent with the seed (which corresponds to the incenter-only case), and hold whether the excenter-induced segment lies outside the triangle (the length is still well-defined). The verifier implements these formulas and reduces the rational values to lowest terms, returning m+n+p+q. The generator enforces valid scalene triangles and nontrivial fractional outputs to maintain difficulty.

Implementation notes: Variables in the wrapper use AB={ab}, AC={ac}, BC={bc}. Internally, the verifier renames a=BC, b=AC, c=AB. Fraction reduction uses gcd, and several constraints (scalene, non-integer outputs, denominators within bounds) help keep instances both valid and nontrivial.
source_question: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB=21$ , $AC=22$ and $BC=20$ . Points $D$ and $E$ are located on $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ , respectively, such that $\overline{DE}$ is parallel to $\overline{BC}$ and contains the center of the inscribed circle of triangle $ABC$ . Then $DE=\frac{m}{n}$ , where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $m+n$ .
